anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: Holy ground: no covering of deadness (the hide shoe).
Quoted: having shod your feet in readiness of the gospel.

pass_a_gloss: But these things are not fighting; they are taken of other and other thought. For when someone treads holy earth, he is commanded to have no deadness in himself, no longer being about to cover some deadness of his; but when he chews the pascha, he is commanded to eat with haste for the sake of being ready, as also the apostle teaches saying: Having shod your feet in readiness of the gospel.
pass_b_english: But these things are not at war. They are taken according to one thought and another. For when someone treads holy ground, he is commanded to have no deadness in himself, no longer about to cover any deadness of his. But when he chews the Passover, he is commanded to eat in haste for the sake of being ready, as the apostle also teaches, saying: "Having shod your feet in readiness of the gospel."
source_text: Ἀλλὰ ταῦτα οὐ μαχόμενά ἐστιν, ἑτέρας δὲ καὶ ἑτέρας ἐπινοίας λαμβανόμενα· ὅτε γὰρ ἁγίαν τις πατεῖ γῆν, οὐδεμίαν νεκρότητα ἐν αὐτῷ ἔχειν κελεύεται οὐδέτι μέλλων αὐτοῦ νεκρότητά τινα περικαλύπτειν, ὅτε δὲ τρώγει τὸ πάσχα, κελεύεται μετὰ σπουδῆς ἐσθίειν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἕτοιμος εἶναι, ὡς καὶ ὁ ἀπόστολος διδάσκει λέγων· "Ὑποδησάμενοι τοὺς πόδας ὑμῶν ἐν ἑτοιμασίᾳ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου".
